newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - SKW Trostberg says it buying Sandoz's MBT.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - SKW Trostberg says it buying Sandoz's MBT.

text.p: German SKW Trostberg AG said on Monday it plans to buy Master Builders Technologies (MBT) from Swiss group Sandoz AG, creating one of the world's leading suppliers of construction chemical products and systems.
After months of speculation, the German specialty chemicals group revealed that it had signed an agreement with Sandoz to buy the Zurich-based MBT group for 1.3 billion Swiss francs ($1.1 billion).
The deal, still requiring anti-trust authority approval, is expected to be completed during the fourth quarter of 1996, Sandoz said in a statement issued in Basle.

SKW Trostberg, until now a niche player specialising in building industry chemicals and food additives, beat several contenders for MBT. Sandoz needed to sell the group to clear the way to form Norvatis with rival Ciba-Geigy AG, a source said.

"Clearly this is a major acquisition for SKW Trostberg but it will work very well and with it SKW Trostberg will become a global speciality chemicals company," Michele Colocci, Vice President at JP Morgan, advisors to SKW Trostberg told Reuters.
Analysts, who welcomed the deal, said the MBT would allow SKW Trostberg to extend its reach into the U.S. and Japanese marekts, rounding out its geographical presence.

Separately SKW Trostberg, majority owned by German industrial group VIAG AG, said pre-tax profits jumped 62 percent to 131 million marks during the first half of the year while sales rose 12 percent to 2.1 billion marks.

Looking ahead, SKW Trostberg predicted full year pre-tax profits would rise by about 30 percent, extending 1995's strong results when operating profit surged 66 percent to 280 million marks and sales rose 72 percent to 3.86 billion marks.
The stock market also welcomed the news, sending its shares 3.5 percent higher to 39.40 marks in Frankfurt bourse trading while the broader market was flat.
Dealers said they were particularly relieved to hear that SKW Trostberg was not planning to raise capital to finance the sizeable acquisition.
"SKW Trostberg is in a position to manage (the takeover) in under its own power," SKW Trostberg management board chairman Wilhelm Simson told a news conference in Munich.
Analysts suggested the financing for the deal would provide little worries for SKW Trostberg, particularly as it still enjoyed the backing of its parent Viag.

Although Simson ruled out a near-term capital rise, he said the topic may be considered next year when the group may want to generate new funds needed to finance its strategy of growing through a string of acquisitions.
Sources close to the company said one option was to float more shares in the group after its initial public offering last spring was well received.
New money, analysts speculated, may then be used to either buy a fourth business line or make a few strategic acquisitions in the three existing core areas.

SKW Trostberg has aggressively searched for acquisitions, buying French SBI Systems Bio-Industries for 1.2 billion marks to strengthen the food additives unit in 1995 and taking over the construction chemicals unit from Austria's DSM Chemie in May.
